title: Span Beacon — Anchored Thread Navigator & Correlation Lens
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Introduce an anchor-first drilldown workspace for request sessions: a lightweight, left-anchored 'Span Beacon' panel that pins a chosen span or correlation ID and surfaces related threads, sibling spans, and filtered timeline tracks. The goal is to let engineers and SREs maintain focus on a single causal anchor while exploring related requests, latency anomalies, and KV-cache hot-paths without losing context. This feature complements existing session search by enabling persistent anchors, quick comparisons across spans, and inline metric overlays (token counts, GPU time, retry counts).
comments: 2026-02-20 — Kickoff: scoped initial hypothesis and primary use-cases with PM and Eng (investigate slow tail, correlation drift, cross-model fallbacks). Decided to prioritize single-anchor UX over multi-anchor for MVP to reduce cognitive overhead.

2026-02-24 — Early sketches: two-pane layout (left anchor lane + right timeline canvas) tested internally. PM prefers compact anchor header that survives navigation; Eng flagged concerns around rendering large span trees at 200ms polling.

2026-02-28 — Prototype v0.1 created in Figma; added affordances: 'pin span', 'snap to child', correlation badge with copy-to-clipboard, and heat-strip for per-span latency. UX research session scheduled.

2026-03-03 — Usability feedback: developers appreciated anchor persistence and the compare-to-anchor overlay. Observability team asked for an optional toggle to show raw trace IDs and to integrate with current waterfall view.

2026-03-07 — Engineering review: recommended lazy-loading deep spans, virtualized span list, and server-side correlation indexing. Noted requirement for API changes (trace API: include parent pointer and KV-cache annotations).
2026-03-11 — Accessibility pass: ensured keyboard focus flows for anchor pin/unpin, aria-labels for timeline markers, and color-contrast adjustments for heat-strip.
review_feedback: PM (Diego Martinez) — strong alignment on SLO debugging flow; ask to add 'compare to baseline' toggle that overlays median latency for selected service.
Eng (Priya Shah) — prefer server-side pagination for sibling spans; flag: avoid client-side rehydration of massive KV caches.
Observability lead (Marcus Chen) — request ability to pin multiple correlation badges for cross-session stitching in future iterations.
Security (Olivia Park) — reminder to hide plaintext user tokens in span metadata and to surface KMS-protected fields with a lock icon; recommend a threat model review if we include payload snippets.
decisions: MVP will support a single anchored span or correlation ID per workspace to reduce complexity.
Timeline will prioritize 'snap-to-anchor' + compare-overlay instead of full multi-anchor viewport for first release.
Lazy-load deep-span children with a server cursor; client will provide 'expand all' hint but not fetch by default.
Metric overlays (token count, model name, GPU-ms) are included as lightweight badges and optional toggles.
Expose a compact 'copy correlation ID' action in the anchor header for easy cross-tool navigation.
Hide any sensitive payload fields by default; show a redacted preview with an explicit 'reveal' action that logs access for audit.
next_steps: Finalize high-fidelity screens for anchor header and compare-overlay (owner: design, due 2026-03-14).
Eng to prototype server-side cursor and correlation index endpoints (owner: ENG, dependency ticket ENG-33450).
Add telemetry events spec for anchor interactions and compare toggles to instrumentation backlog (owner: Observability).
Run two 90-minute follow-up usability sessions with backend engineers and SREs to validate navigation and keyboard flows (scheduled 2026-03-16).
Prepare release notes blurb and in-app tour outline for rollout (owner: PM).
